elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty only says "any services performed by the PG will be free from defects for a period of thirty (30) days following performance" — there is no professional-and-workmanlike standard anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "any software supplied in connection with APCN 2 will conform to its documentation for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Period is "ninety (90) days following delivery", not 12 months; the drafter deliberately targeted the fallback duration.
Services period is "thirty (30) days following performance", short of the preferred 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "The remedy for breach of this warranty shall be repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or services".
"...or a refund of the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered operative language; the rationale asserts Paragraph 25 covers it, but that paragraph is not cited or rendered, so it cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no malicious-code warranty, and the retained disclaimer negates any implied one.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted warranty (i): software "will conform to its documentation for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" — meets the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted warranty (ii): services "will be free from defects for a period of thirty (30) days following performance" — meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "...shall be repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or services".
"...or a refund of the fees paid for them."

reasons: Finding status is correct: the document was at walk-away (4.9 disclaims all representations and warranties and directs that "nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty"), and Subparagraph 4.8 gives only a discretionary PG right to pursue the Suppliers, not a remedy running to us. An insertion was the right response.

All four fallback elements are met in operative language: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund of fees paid. Preferred is not met (90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 rather than 90 days for services, no professional-and-workmanlike standard, no malicious-code warranty, and compliance with laws unverifiable from the rendered text).

Minimality is satisfied: the edit adds only the warranty sentence and the two carve-out phrases needed to stop the retained disclaimer swallowing it; no survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure, damages category or other extra requirement was added, and no favourable existing wording was deleted.

Intent fails on a dangling cross-reference: both carve-outs read "except as expressly provided in Subparagraph 4.10", but the inserted warranty paragraph is rendered unnumbered, so no Subparagraph 4.10 exists. Repair by numbering the inserted paragraph "4.10" (or re-pointing both carve-outs to the actual inserted subparagraph number).

Consequence of that defect in substance: with the carve-out pointing nowhere, the retained closing words of 4.9 ("nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty or guarantee") can be read to negate the new software/Wet Segment-related warranty, leaving the two provisions contradictory rather than reconciled as the comment claims.
